packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-08 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

EXPOSURE / RULES STATEMENT
Nothing in my context proposed an identification of this fragment or a reading of
it. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..006 of this packet (plus the reader
brief). No web, no search, no packet.json, no image processing. I do not name a
work or author below; where the scribe himself writes a reference label I
transcribe it as written.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- image-001: overview of one face of a small horizontal strip, about 95 x 30 mm by
  the ruler, upright, on black felt with a "B" label. Tiles image-002 (left half)
  and image-003 (right half) overlap by a few letters in the middle.
- image-004: overview of the other face (same "B" label). Tiles image-005 (left
  half) and image-006 (right half), overlapping in the middle.
- Each face carries six full lines of a small, compact gothic book hand in dark
  ink, plus the tops of a seventh line along the lower cut. The upper cut passes
  just above line 1 (a notch/hole in the top edge removes a few letters of line 1
  on both faces). The left and right edges are cuts: lines begin and end mid-word,
  so the strip is from the interior of a column or page; I cannot tell from these
  crops whether the layout was one or two columns, and no margin, running title or
  gloss is visible.
- Heavily abbreviated prose. Points separate clauses and set off numerals.
- Red: on the first face a red-filled initial or paraph in line 1 (image-003, top),
  marking a new unit that begins with an ordinal word; on the second face, red
  touches on the capitals "E" (image-005 l.5) and "Q" (image-006 l.6).
- Underlining: a thin pen line runs under part of first-face lines 3-5 (visible
  under "xx", under "se." and under the reference in l.5). It may mark the cited
  passages; it could also be ruling. Tentative.
- No interlinear gloss. Small superscript letters are ordinary abbreviation.
- Tentative interpretation: continuous expository prose built from short
  authority-citations, each introduced by "de quo dicitur" or an abbreviated
  source label. The second face is fainter (probably the paste-down or flesh
  side) and less secure.
- Which face is recto is not determinable.

SPANS SELECTED
The fragment is small enough to give every line of both faces. Unread: only the
decapitated seventh line on each face, and the few letters lost in the top notch.

TRANSCRIPTION
Line numbers are counted from the top of each tile image; in this packet they are
the same in the overview, the left tile and the right tile. I give each line as
left tile | right tile, with the join marked "|"; letters repeated in the overlap
are given once.

FIRST FACE (image-001; image-002 = left, image-003 = right)
l.1  image-002: ]q(ui) dix(it) . a(n)i(m)a m(e)a h(abe)s m(u)lta [notch: 2-3 letters lost]
     image-003: ]a(?) (et) c(etera) . [red-filled initial or paraph] T(er)cio(?) ad h(oc) p(ro)pt(er)(?)[
     (written: "q dix. aia ma hs mlta[..]a 7 c." ; after the red mark "tcio"/"tao" then
     "ad h" with hook, then "p" with crossed descender + "pt" and a final hook)
l.2  image-002: ]ptu(m)(?) nos moue(re) d(ebet) q(uia) (est) da(m)pno|
     image-003: |sa c(re)ato(?)re(m) suu(m) obli[
     (first word: "-ptu" or "-ctu" with stroke; "dapnosa" with stroke over p; the word
     before "suu(m)" is written c/e + l-like stroke + "ore" with stroke: "creatorem"
     is a proposal, "elatorem"/"elationem" not excluded)
l.3  image-002: ]ce(n)tib(us)(?) penis . de q(u)o d(icitu)r . xx . |
     image-003: | Reuelab(un)t celi i(n)iq(ui)tate(m)(?)[
     (the last word is written as i + minims/t + a with strokes above; "iniquitatem"
     is a proposal from the shape; "xx" stands between two points and may be a
     chapter number)
l.4  image-002: ]a (con)surg(et) adu(er)sus eu(m) . se(quitur)(?) . |
     image-003: | det(ra)het(ur)(?) in die furoris[
     (written "se" with superscript mark, then "det" + superscript + "het" + hook)
l.5  image-002: ](et) h(oc) (est) p(rimu)s(?) . ip(s)i(us)(?) ad° . ex(emplum)(?) . luc(e)(?) . de d|
     image-003: |iuite q(ui) i(n)dueba(tur) p(ur)p(ur)[
     (the first four short words are bare sigla: tironian et, "h" with hook, the
     "est" sign, a capital P with 9-hook, "ip" with stroke + 3-shaped sign, "ad"
     with superscript o; I cannot resolve them with confidence. "ex. luc." each with
     abbreviation mark. Line ends "p" with two superscript marks, cut)
l.6  image-002: ]a (et) bysso (et) e(pulabatur)(?) co(tidie)(?) sple(ndide) . de q(u)o d(icitu)r q(uod) |
     image-003: | mortu(us) (est) (et) sep(u)lt(us)[
     (written "7 bysso 7 e. co. sple." with single-letter suspensions for the two
     middle words; expansions of those two are proposals only)
l.7  [tops of letters along the cut; not readable]

SECOND FACE (image-004; image-005 = left, image-006 = right) - fainter, less secure
l.1  image-005: ]in t(er)ra(m)(?) car(n)is(?) . q(uia) illic [notch] |
     image-006: | [..]cor(?) car(n)is(?) ign(?)e(?) n(ost)r(u)m(?) i(n)cend[
     (rubbed; "in" + "t" with marks; a word "cari-"/"carn-" twice; "q" with 2-shaped
     sign; "illic"; after the notch "-cor" with hook; last word begins "icc/ice" +
     "d")
l.2  image-005: ]apostate(?) ang(e)li . Hinc (er)g(o) io|
     image-006: |sue cepit asor(?) q(ua)n(do)(?)[
     (written "g" with superscript o; then "iosue" clearly; "cepit"; a short word
     "asor"/"afor"; "qn" with stroke)
l.3  image-005: ]di s(un)t(?) decreto(?) dya(bol)o(?) co(m)pla|
     image-006: |n[..]t (et) in ip(s)o(rum)(?) cartho(?)[ / carbo(?)[
     (the second word after "di" is a long word beginning "de" and ending "-to";
     "dya" with superscript o)
l.4  image-005: ]ge(m)mis(?) (et) si(?) p(er)cussit om(ne)s |
     image-006: | a(n)i(m)as q(ua)n(do) eas(?) inflam(m)a[
l.5  image-005: ]in amore s(uo)(?) . Et [E touched red] b(e)n(e) dic(itu)r(?) . p|
     image-006: |(er)cussit a(n)i(m)as(?) . q(uia) hii(?) p(er)cu[
     (written "bn" with stroke + "digt"/"dicit"; the word after "p(er)cussit" is
     rubbed, with a small dark spot after it)
l.6  image-005: ]uuln(er)a n(on) sentiu(n)t cor(por)is(?) : s(ed) c|
     image-006: |orda(?) . Q(ui)a [Q touched red] a(utem) ista p(er)cussi[
     (written "cor" with hook and a punctus elevatus, "s" + 3-sign, "corda" or
     "cordis")
l.7  [tops of letters along the cut; not readable]

Most secure sequences, for a later check:
- first face: "... dix(it) . anima mea habes multa ... et cetera . [red] ... ad hoc";
  "nos mouere debet"; "da(m)pnosa"; "penis . de quo dicitur . xx . Reuelabunt celi";
  "consurget aduersus eum"; "in die furoris"; "luc. de diuite qui induebatur";
  "et bysso"; "sple(ndide) . de quo dicitur quod mortuus est et sepultus".
- second face: "angeli . Hinc ergo iosue cepit"; "percussit omnes animas";
  "inflam(m)a-"; "in amore"; "Et ... percussit"; "uulnera non sentiunt ... sed
  cord-"; "Quia autem ista percussi-".

LIMITATIONS
- Every line is cut at both ends; the amount lost on each side is unknown.
- Line 1 of each face loses a few letters to the notch in the top edge; line 7 is
  only letter-tops.
- Tiles are low resolution (about 700 px for half the strip), so individual
  abbreviation marks are at the limit of what can be told apart; all expansions
  in parentheses are proposals, and those with (?) are weak.
- The second face is abraded and faint throughout, lines 1-4 especially.
- I did not determine recto/verso or the order of the two faces.
- Suggested additional view: a higher-resolution scan of the second face
  (or UV), and any sibling strips from the same binding (the "B" label suggests
  there is at least an "A").
